title: Harmonic Hardy Classes and Fatou Boundary Limits

items.title: Poisson integral of a finite complex boundary measure
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Identify T=R/Z with the unit circle and write m for normalized arclength. For a finite regular complex Borel measure μ on T define P[μ](z)=∫_T (1−|z|²)/|ζ−z|² dμ(ζ). For f∈L¹(T,m), P[f] means P[f m]; this is independent of the representative and agrees with the earlier real continuous-data integral.
items.strategy: The kernel is bounded continuous on T for each fixed z, so the finite complex-measure integral exists; a.e. equal L¹ densities induce the same measure. Check the angular normalization against the published Poisson kernel and torus Haar integral.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: Harmonic Hardy classes on the unit disc
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For 1≤p<∞, h^p(D) consists of complex-valued functions whose real and imaginary parts are harmonic and for which sup_{0≤r<1}||u_r||_{L^p(T,m)}<∞, where u_r(ζ)=u(rζ). For p=∞ use sup_{r<1}||u_r||_∞, equal to sup_{z∈D}|u(z)| because each u_r is continuous. These suprema are the h^p norms.
items.strategy: Use the published componentwise convention for complex harmonicity and normalized torus measure; continuity on each compact circle makes essential and pointwise suprema agree at p=∞.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: Poisson extension is an Lp contraction and converges in finite Lp
items.statement: Assume countable choice. If 1≤p≤∞ and f∈L^p(T,m;C), then P[f] is complex harmonic, lies in h^p(D), and ||P_r*f||_p≤||f||_p for every 0≤r<1. If p<∞, ||P_r*f−f||_p→0 as r↑1. No L∞ norm convergence is asserted for arbitrary data.
items.strategy: Verify directly that the Poisson kernel is harmonic in its disc variable, then use local derivative bounds and dominated convergence to differentiate under the finite L¹ integral and prove componentwise harmonicity. Positivity and unit mass give |P_r*f|≤P_r*|f|; apply real Jensen to t↦t^p and Fubini with translation invariance of m, or the sup estimate at infinity. Approximate finite-p f by continuous torus functions, use the contraction on the error, and apply the published uniform Poisson approximation to real and imaginary parts.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: h1 is isometric to finite regular complex boundary measures
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every u∈h¹(D) has a unique finite regular complex Borel measure μ on T with u=P[μ]. Conversely every such μ gives an h¹ function, ||u||_{h¹}=|μ|(T), and u_r m converges weak-star to μ against C(T) as r↑1. A general h¹ function need not have an L¹ density.
items.strategy: AC supplies the ultrafilter lemma for the published separable-predual weak-star subsequence theorem and DC for complex Riesz–Markov. C(T) is separable by rational-coefficient trigonometric polynomials. Extract a weak-star limit μ of u_{r_j}m for r_j↑1. Apply the published Poisson representation to u on each smaller closed disc and pass to the limit against the continuous Poisson kernel to get u=P[μ]. Conversely Fubini, positivity and unit mass give ||(P[μ])_r||_1≤|μ|(T); test against a continuous g, move the kernel to g, and use uniform approximation to prove u_r m→μ weak-star. The dual norm of C(T) equals variation, giving equality and uniqueness.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: h^p is the Poisson image of Lp for 1<p≤∞
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For 1<p≤∞ every complex u∈h^p(D) is P[f] for a unique f∈L^p(T,m;C), and ||u||_{h^p}=||f||_p. For finite p, u_r→f in L^p; at p=∞ the radial functions converge weak-star against L¹, with no general L∞ norm-limit claim.
items.strategy: For 1<p<∞, choose r_j↑1. AC supplies DC, the ultrafilter lemma and Hahn–Banach for the published reflexive Lp weak-subsequence theorem. Extract u_{r_j}⇀f in Lp. The Poisson formula on the disc of radius r_j and the fact P(z,·)∈Lq let weak convergence identify u(z)=P[f](z). For p=∞ use the h¹ boundary measure μ. The bound |∫g dμ|≤||u||∞∫|g|dm for continuous g extends by L¹ density to a bounded complex L¹ functional; apply the published real L¹–L∞ duality to its two real components and recombine to obtain dμ=f dm. Apply the published complex finite-simple dual norm-recovery lemma to phase tests of this density for the sharp ||f||∞≤||u||∞ bound. Uniqueness follows from finite-p norm convergence or weak-star testing at infinity. The contraction and boundary convergence yield the reverse norm inequality and the stated radial modes.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: Circle maximal function and nontangential approach regions
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For a finite complex Borel measure μ on T, let I_h(ζ) be the open circular arc of radius h centered at ζ for 0<h<1/2, and let I_{1/2}(ζ)=T. Define M_T μ(ζ)=sup_{0<h≤1/2}|μ|(I_h(ζ))/m(I_h(ζ)); for f∈L¹ write M_T f=M_T(fm). For A>1 define Γ_A(ζ)={z∈D:|z−ζ|<A(1−|z|)} and N_Av(ζ)=sup_{z∈Γ_A(ζ)}|v(z)|. A nontangential limit means convergence within every Γ_A as z→ζ.
items.strategy: The whole-circle endpoint h=1/2 includes atoms at the antipode. Check positivity of arc measure, representative independence for f, and the relation between Γ_A and standard Stolz cones.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: The circle maximal function is weak type one one for finite measures
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every finite regular complex Borel measure μ on T and λ>0, the set {ζ:M_T μ(ζ)>λ} is measurable and m({M_T μ>λ})≤3|μ|(T)/λ. In particular the same holds with |μ|(T)=||f||_1 for f∈L¹(T,m).
items.strategy: For fixed arc radius, ζ↦|μ|(I_h(ζ)) is lower semicontinuous by Fatou; hence the superlevel set is open. Cover a compact subset of it by finitely many witnessing centered arcs. Greedily choose pairwise disjoint arcs in nonincreasing-radius order; each discarded arc lies in the triple dilation of one selected arc, and normalized arc length satisfies m(3I)≤3m(I), including the whole-circle case. Sum λm(I)<|μ|(I) over the disjoint arcs and then use regularity of m to pass from compact subsets to the whole open set.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: Poisson nontangential maximal function is controlled by circle maximal averages
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every finite regular complex measure μ, every A>1 and every ζ∈T, N_A(P[μ])(ζ)≤(A+1)² M_T μ(ζ). In particular N_A(P[f])(ζ)≤(A+1)² M_T f(ζ) for f∈L¹.
items.strategy: For radial rζ, the positive Poisson kernel is decreasing in circular distance from ζ; approximate it from above by positive linear combinations of indicators of centered arcs and use its unit mass to get |P[μ](rζ)|≤M_T μ(ζ). If z∈Γ_A(ζ) and r=|z|, the geometry gives |rζ−η|≤(A+1)|z−η| for every η∈T, so P(z,η)≤(A+1)²P(rζ,η). Integrate against |μ| and combine the two estimates. Treat r=0 directly.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: Fatou limits for Poisson extensions of L1 boundary data
items.statement: Assume countable choice. If f∈L¹(T,m;C), then P[f](z)→f(ζ) for m-almost every ζ as z→ζ in every fixed nontangential region Γ_A(ζ), A>1. The assertion uses an a.e. representative of f and makes no claim about arbitrary tangential paths.
items.strategy: For each A and ζ define the limsup error. Its measurability follows by restricting the continuous interior function P[f] to a countable dense set of interior points and using Borel cone-membership sets. The error is zero for continuous data by the disc Dirichlet theorem, componentwise. Approximate f in L¹ by g∈C(T); bound the limsup error by (A+1)²M_T(f−g)+|f−g|. The local weak (1,1) inequality and Chebyshev make each positive superlevel set null as ||f−g||_1→0. Intersect the full-measure sets for integer A≥2 to obtain every finite aperture.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: Bounded harmonic functions have L-infinity Fatou boundary data
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every bounded complex harmonic u on D is P[f] for a unique f in L-infinity(T,m), with ||u||_{h-infinity}=sup_{z in D}|u(z)|=||f||_infinity, and u(z) tends to f(zeta) nontangentially for m-almost every zeta.
items.strategy: Apply the p=∞ representation theorem. Since m(T)=1, f∈L∞ lies in L¹; apply the L¹ Fatou theorem. AC is carried from the representation theorem, where it supplies the published compactness and measure-duality inputs.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137

items.title: Positive harmonic boundary measures and compact normalized families
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A nonnegative real harmonic u on D is P[μ] for a unique finite nonnegative regular Borel measure μ on T, with μ(T)=u(0); conversely every such μ gives a nonnegative harmonic function. Every sequence of nonnegative harmonic functions with u_n(0)=1 has a subsequence converging locally uniformly to a nonnegative harmonic function normalized at zero.
items.strategy: The circle mean-value property gives ||u_r||_1=u(0), so apply the h¹ measure representation. Its weak-star radial limit of positive measures is positive by testing nonnegative continuous functions; the mass is u(0) by the constant test. For a normalized sequence, the measures are probabilities. AC supplies weak-star sequential compactness of the dual ball of separable C(T). Weak-star convergence gives pointwise convergence of Poisson integrals; uniform continuity of (z,ζ)↦P(z,ζ) on each compact K×T and a finite epsilon-net upgrade it to uniform convergence on K. Positivity and normalization pass to the limit.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

title: Harmonic Hardy Classes and Fatou Boundary Limits: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Poisson extension of an indicator arc
items.statement: For a nonempty proper open arc I⊂T and f=1_I, u=P[f] satisfies 0<u<1, ||u_r||_1=m(I), and ||u_r||_p≤m(I)^{1/p} for finite p. Its nontangential boundary value is 1 at interior points of I and 0 at interior points of its complement; at each endpoint its radial limit is 1/2. The indicator itself has no two-sided pointwise boundary limit at either endpoint.
items.strategy: Positivity and unit mass give the strict bounds and mean-value/Fubini gives the L¹ equality. Apply contraction for other p. The kernel approximate identity gives convergence off the endpoints; at an endpoint split a small symmetric arc into two equal halves, use evenness of P_r, and show the remote opposite endpoint contributes vanishing mass.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: A boundary atom gives an h1 function without an L1 density
items.statement: For ζ0∈T, u(z)=P(z,ζ0)=P[δ_{ζ0}](z) is positive and harmonic, belongs to h¹ with ||u||_{h¹}=1, and has no representing L¹ density. It tends to zero at every other boundary point, while u(rζ0)=(1+r)/(1−r)→∞.
items.strategy: The Poisson kernel has circle mean one, and the h¹ representation theorem identifies the unique boundary measure as δ_{ζ0}, singular to m. On compact arcs away from ζ0 the kernel tends uniformly to zero; the radial formula at ζ0 is explicit.

references.title: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 6, pp. 111–120 and 128–137
Herbert Koch, Notes for Harmonic and Real Analysis, Ch. 3 §§1.2–3, pp. 35–37

items.title: A radial Poisson limit does not control a tangential path
items.statement: There is f∈L∞(T,m), taking only values 0 and 1, whose boundary values have no pointwise limit at ζ=1, such that P[f](r)→0 as r↑1 but P[f](z_n)≥c>0 along a sequence z_n→1 with |z_n−1|/(1−|z_n|)→∞. Thus radial convergence at one point does not extend to arbitrary tangential approaches; this does not contradict Fatou’s almost-everywhere nontangential theorem.
items.strategy: Take disjoint arcs centered at angles t_n=2^(−n) with angular half-width w_n=2^(−3n), n≥3, and let f be their indicator. For r=1−ε use P_r(t)≤Cε/(ε²+t²) and split the arc sum at t_n≈ε to obtain P[f](r)=O(ε). At z_n=(1−w_n)e^{it_n}, integrate the Poisson kernel on the central half of the nth arc to get a fixed positive lower bound. The approach ratio is comparable to t_n/w_n→∞; f(t_n)=1 while f vanishes at intervening angles.
